title: 2008 HMMT February Geometry Problem 9
statement: Let \(A B C\) be a triangle, and \(I\) its incenter. Let the incircle of \(A B C\) touch side \(B C\) at \(D\), and let lines \(B I\) and \(C I\) meet the circle with diameter \(A I\) at points \(P\) and \(Q\), respectively. Given \(B I=\) \(6, C I=5, D I=3\), determine the value of \((D P / D Q)^{2}\).

solutions.text: \(\qquad\) Let the incircle touch sides \(A C\) and \(A B\) at \(E\) and \(F\) respectively. Note that \(E\) and \(F\) both lie on the circle with diameter \(A I\) since \(\angle A E I=\angle A F I=90^{\circ}\). The key observation is that \(D, E, P\) are collinear. To prove this, suppose that \(P\) lies outside the triangle (the other case is analogous), then \(\angle P E A=\angle P I A=\angle I B A+\angle I A B=\frac{1}{2}(\angle B+\angle A)=90^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2} \angle C=\angle D E C\), which implies that \(D, E, P\) are collinear. Similarly \(D, F, Q\) are collinear. Then, by Power of a Point, \(D E \cdot D P=D F \cdot D Q\). So \(D P / D Q=D F / D E\). Now we compute \(D F / D E\). Note that \(D F=2 D B \sin \angle D B I=2 \sqrt{6^{2}-3^{2}}\left(\frac{3}{6}\right)=3 \sqrt{3}\), and \(D E=\) \(2 D C \sin \angle D C I=2 \sqrt{5^{2}-3^{2}}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)=\frac{24}{5}\). Therefore, \(D F / D E=\frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{8}\). [One or more solution diagrams were omitted from this imported transcription.]
